question: Does model-specific budget calibration produce more groups with both correct and incorrect answers than a development-selected global budget, and what does calibration cost?

scope.supporting_scope: Historical development analysis and integration demonstration only.
scope.inference_scope: Pilot on the admitted miniature labs and one recorded model configuration.
scope.training_claim: Reward variation is a diagnostic; no RL training or learning improvement is established.

historical_baseline.use: Development evidence only; never pool historical scores with release grades.

execution_limits.generation_and_repair: Separate subscription usage, logged per invocation; local CPU only.
execution_limits.quota_handling: Checkpoint and pause; do not change model, skip difficult labs, or consume more than the episode cap.

requires: Passing grading, isolation, budget, and discovery regressions
Four development claim-lab IDs selected by the rule below
Resolved requested model ID and reported model ID, CLI version, and decoding controls or explicit unavailability
Exact prompt text, rendering code, runtime lock, task/grader code, and charging-schedule hashes
Successful smoke checks on development labs only
Frozen baseline policy and shared answer-estimator code hashes
Frozen generation, triage, repair, and admission rules and prompt hashes
Archived fresh metadata response, selection date, ordered first 16 candidate IDs, and paper versions

lock_schedule.before: Fresh model pilots or inspection of confirmation outcomes
requires: Human fidelity reviews completed without fresh model scores
Ordered admission funnel and first eight eligible claim-lab IDs, or the smaller actual cohort
Qualification labels and fixed effect margins
Exact lab, space, seed-partition, task, charging-schedule, and runtime hashes
A protocol-bound manifest with all membership decisions

lock_schedule.before: Any fresh confirmation rollout or inspection of confirmation outcomes
requires: All pilot attempt records and calibration decisions or recorded fallbacks
Frozen arm budgets, group descriptors, and planned rollout slots

binding_policy.purpose: Record the exact artifacts required by each lock; this specification does not claim those artifacts already exist.
binding_policy.mutation_rule: Append dated lock records with hashes before the affected data are observed. Never overwrite an earlier lock.
binding_policy.model_change: Stop if the resolved model changes; do not pool configurations in the primary analysis.
binding_policy.protocol_change: Preserve this version and record an amendment, rationale, timing, and affected observations. Post-outcome changes are exploratory.

development.reference_selection: Coverage-oriented manual selection from historical labs before new model scores; overlap of mechanisms is allowed.
development.claim_selection: First four reference labs in lexicographic environment-ID order that pass human admission and have a qualified claim under the corrected grader. If fewer than four qualify, stop and amend before budget-selection rollouts.
development.selection_basis: Human review and corrected qualification data only; never new model performance.
development.qualification_data: Historical held-out seeds with corrected grading, explicitly labeled development-only; no independent-confirmation claim.
development.smoke_rule: At most six episodes on development labs, covering all three budgets; exclude them from budget selection and confirmation.

fresh_cohort.date_rule: At candidate lock, use the most recent completed UTC first-publication date with at least one unseen paper in the primary categories. An empty date may be skipped using metadata only.
fresh_cohort.freshness_rule: Exclude papers previously generated or manually reviewed in this project; record the exclusion list before selecting candidates.
fresh_cohort.ordering: Deduplicate by versionless arXiv ID, retain the fetched version, sort IDs numerically ascending, and take the first 16. No relevance or model-performance reranking.
fresh_cohort.metadata_failure: Pause and retry retrieval of the same date; do not choose another date because downloads fail.
eligibility: Pure Python CPU lab with synthetic or locally bundled data; no downloads, pretrained weights, or paid services
A concrete paper mechanism and a fair treatment/baseline comparison documented by a human reviewer
Discrete complete paired grid with fixed metric direction and meaningful-effect margin
Passing sandbox, determinism, completeness, cache-version, and lab-specific invariant checks
A settled claim on the qualification split under the release grader
fresh_cohort.effect_margin: Set and justify from the metric and task meaning before inspecting qualification outcomes. Never tune the margin to admit a preferred label.
fresh_cohort.membership: First eight accepted candidates with qualified claims in the archived candidate order; stop generation once eight qualify or all 16 are processed.
fresh_cohort.accounting: Record every candidate as admitted, rejected, needs_review, generation_failed, qualification_ambiguous, or not_processed_after_target.
fresh_cohort.insufficient_cohort: Use the smaller actual cohort without extending the candidate list; with zero gradable labs report no primary comparison.
fresh_cohort.replacement_rule: Never replace a locked lab because of model performance, confirmation instability, or an inconvenient result.

seed_partitions.pairing: Within each split, both treatment arms and every context use the same seed IDs.
seed_partitions.missing_data: Any missing required pair makes that split incomplete; never silently reweight the estimand.

visible_order.rule: List all permutations of the four visible seeds lexicographically. Set k to the integer SHA-256 digest of UTF-8 'benchtop_release_v1/order/' plus lab content hash, modulo 24.
visible_order.pilot: Permutation k, shared across all candidate budgets and repeats within that lab.
visible_order.confirmation: Permutation (k + 1) modulo 24, shared across both arms and all repeats within that lab.
visible_order.interpretation: A changed ordering is not a new research problem; model repeats use independent sessions, not claimed independent underlying worlds.

grading.contrast: Orient the metric so higher is better. For each seed average treatment-minus-baseline across all contexts with equal weights; estimate the mean and standard error across these seed means.

interval.degrees_of_freedom: number of paired seed means minus one

decision.no_meaningful_difference: lower endpoint > -min_effect AND upper endpoint < min_effect
decision.ambiguous: Any other complete-data case, including equality at a decision boundary

bootstrap_diagnostic.unit: Whole seed blocks, preserving treatment pairing and cross-context dependence
bootstrap_diagnostic.interval: Percentile 2.5 and 97.5; report diagnostic disagreement without changing primary membership

grading.pilot_truth: Qualification label; used only by the evaluator and calibration selector.
grading.confirmation_truth: Independent confirmation label, inspected only after cohort and arm decisions are locked.
grading.confirmation_stability: Gradable only if confirmation is complete, settled, and agrees with qualification. Otherwise retain the lab in the full-cohort denominator and mark model reward comparisons unavailable.
grading.reward: 1 for a correct claim answer, otherwise 0, only on gradable tasks. Missing infrastructure outcomes remain missing.
grading.where_scope: Supporting analysis only; state graded levels and pointwise interval coverage without implying simultaneous coverage.

agent.model_binding: Resolve and pin the available model before development budget selection; record reported IDs per attempt. If unavailable, amend the model choice before evaluation.
agent.tool_access: Only the episode-scoped MCP capability; no built-in tools, arbitrary shell, browser, filesystem, extra MCP servers, admin routes, or arbitrary network access.
agent.sessions: Fresh model session for every attempt; no session persistence or conversation reuse.
agent.prompt_binding: Freeze system text, first-message template, lab-description renderer, CLI configuration, and code hashes before development budget selection; keep the template and information access constant across arms.
agent.sampling: Record supported decoding settings. Unsupported temperature and model random-seed controls are explicitly unavailable, not assumed fixed.
agent.submission: First valid answer is final. One format-only correction is allowed; repeated submissions receive only an idempotent receipt. Rewards and hidden seed data never enter the agent conversation.

budget.denominator: Frozen sum of per-configuration charged costs multiplied by the four visible seeds.
budget.charging_schedule: One versioned per-configuration estimate measured on development or qualification execution and frozen before rollouts; the same estimates are visible to all policies and the LLM.
budget.separation: Charged experimental budget is distinct from actual cached wall time, unique execution work, and model inference cost.
budget.live_failures: No experimental-result charge for failed runs; failures consume the bounded call/retry allowance and actual work is still logged.

baselines.optional_rule: Declare inclusion or deferral at candidate lock, based on development correctness and scope; never fresh scores.
baselines.majority_rule: Use the four development claim labels; break ties in primary_labels order and freeze before fresh pilots.
baselines.estimator: One shared answer estimator for the main classical-policy comparison; define its weighting, pairing, and missing-context treatment on development data and freeze the code before fresh replay.
baselines.information_rule: Same visible observations, question, public cost estimates, budget and call limits; no hidden table lookup, qualification reward, or confirmation reward during acquisition.
baselines.label_use: Hidden labels are used after a baseline finishes only for scoring, never experimental selection.
baselines.weighting: Cost preference must not redefine an equal-context target as a cheap-context target.
baselines.historical_traces: Common-estimator reconstruction is retrospective and limited to complete observed-data traces.

calibration.completed_outcome_rule: Agent-failure zero rewards count toward completed pilot outcomes; unresolved infrastructure attempts do not. Require all four planned slots before selection.
calibration.posterior: Beta(correct + 1, valid completed pilot outcomes - correct + 1)
calibration.objective: 1 - E[p^8] - E[(1-p)^8] under the pilot posterior
calibration.tie_rule: Choose the smallest budget with objective >= maximum objective minus 0.05.
calibration.global_control: Average the objective across the four development labs at each budget and apply the same near-best/smallest-budget rule. This budget is fixed before fresh generation.

fallbacks.no_observed_mixed_budget: If every budget has either zero correct or four correct pilots, use the global control budget and retain the diagnostic.
fallbacks.incomplete_pilots: If any candidate budget lacks four completed outcomes after permitted retry, use the global control budget and mark calibration incomplete.

calibration.pilot_reuse: Never include pilot or development outcomes in confirmation groups.

confirmation.same_budget_case: Retain separate independent model sessions and planned slots even when both arms choose the same budget.
confirmation.ordering: In cohort order, alternate arms for each replicate, reversing the starting arm on odd-numbered lab indices. Dispatch at most two sessions concurrently.
confirmation.controls: Identical model configuration, prompt template, paper visibility, visible ordering, tool limits, charging schedule, and grader; arm budget alone may differ.
confirmation.baseline_comparison: Reuse the global-budget confirmation arm for matched-budget comparison with classical replay; no additional model batch.

episode_accounting.cap_rule: Count every invoked rollout model session, including failed or retried sessions. Smaller cohorts reduce planned work. Generation and classical table replay are recorded separately.

identities.canonical_encoding: UTF-8 JSON with sorted object keys, separators ',' and ':', ensure_ascii=false, allow_nan=false; preserve array order.
identities.protocol_hash: SHA-256 of canonical encoding of this entire specification.
identities.bindings_hash: SHA-256 of the immutable phase binding core: resolved artifacts and configuration only, excluding computed IDs, planned slots, and its own hash. Derive group and slot IDs afterward and store the plan hash in a separate lock record referencing this core; no circular hashes.
identities.slot_id: SHA-256 of canonical {group_id, replicate_index}; replicate indices start at zero.
identities.attempt_id: SHA-256 of canonical {slot_id, attempt_index}; attempt zero is the first invocation and one is the only permitted technical retry.
identities.resume: Persist plans before invoking a model. Reconcile server state for in-flight slots. Never rerun a completed valid or agent-failure slot, including an incorrect answer.
identities.deduplication: Independent replicate slots are never deduplicated by episode seed. Preserve all attempts; at most one final usable outcome per slot.

failure_handling.retry_budget: At most 20 retry sessions across the study and always within the 300-start cap.
failure_handling.classification: Use allowlisted machine-readable causes and retained evidence, without consulting whether the answer was correct; unclassified failures remain unresolved, not silently excluded.
failure_handling.after_submission: If an answer was committed before a transport error, reconcile and retain that result instead of replacing the attempt.
failure_handling.incomplete_group: A primary group requires all eight planned outcomes. Unrecovered infrastructure failures make it unavailable; report planned, completed, and unavailable counts.
failure_handling.invalid_lab: Stop the affected lab, preserve evidence and membership, and report unavailable rewards; do not repair a lab after viewing fresh model outcomes for the primary analysis.
failure_handling.sampling_or_timeout_change: Record an amendment and separate exploratory runs; never retroactively remove poor primary attempts.

analysis.primary: Paired difference in the fraction of complete, stable-label groups containing both reward 0 and reward 1, calibrated minus global.
analysis.raw_reporting: For every locked lab and arm publish the eight slot outcomes, selected budget, failure states, and stability state; retain missing entries explicitly.
analysis.denominators: Report all locked qualified labs, stable-label labs, complete paired groups, and unavailable comparisons separately. Primary complete-case results are conditional on stable labels and complete groups.
analysis.no_complete_pairs: Report the primary result and interval as unavailable when no complete gradable lab pair remains; do not substitute a zero effect.
analysis.missing_bounds: Also give worst-case bounds over all locked labs by assigning every unavailable arm's mixed-group indicator either 0 or 1; do not silently improve the denominator.
analysis.baseline: Per-lab global-arm mean accuracy minus each matched-budget classical policy's mean accuracy over 200 replays; average equally across labs.

intervals.unit: Whole labs with both arms and their nested outcomes
intervals.single_lab: Report raw outcomes and no between-lab interval when fewer than two complete labs remain.

analysis.claims: Exploratory pilot with at most eight labs; no equivalence claim, universal generalization, or learning claim. Secondary results are descriptive.
analysis.missing_usage: Use null with an availability reason; never substitute zero for unreported tokens or time.
analysis.efficiency: Include calibration overhead and the measured budget tradeoff. If reporting break-even, state the assumed number of future groups; reward variation alone is not an efficiency benefit.

records.publication: Release sanitized artifacts after scoring is locked. Remove capabilities, credentials and private paths; keep raw transcripts in ignored local state.
